note: Second-generation covalent BTK inhibitors (acalabrutinib, zanubrutinib; orelabrutinib and tirabrutinib without an admissible CLL model comparison); ibrutinib is not a member.
label: CLL/SLL (BTK inhibitors)

engagement.confidence_note: Full text (PMC5548968). Run date of the mouse work not stated; the paper cites the clinical data already public.
engagement.model: CLL mouse models (TCL1 adoptive transfer, NSG primary CLL xenograft)
engagement.note: Acalabrutinib in drinking water held murine BTK occupancy >=90% in TCL1 mice, matching the ~97-99% occupancy already reported in CLL patients.
engagement.quote: Drug occupancy of murine BTK was found to be ≥90% with median occupancy of 96% and 97% after one or four weeks of treatment, respectively
engagement.judgement: Scored as a retrodiction: the paper appeared a year after Byrd 2015 reported human occupancy and itself cites the early clinical activity, so it reproduced a known result.

engagement.magnitude_basis: BTK inhibition moved in both species; no common unit
engagement.confidence_note: Mouse ED50 and human occupancy both from the FDA multidisciplinary review; human occupancy first public in Byrd 2015 (97% predose on 100 mg BID).
engagement.model: Mouse oral-dose BTK PD (occupancy probe, CD69/CD86)
engagement.note: Oral acalabrutinib inhibited mouse B-cell CD69/CD86 (ED50 0.2-1.8 mg/kg); in CLL patients 100 mg BID gave near-complete BTK occupancy. Retrodiction rule: BTK occupancy in patients was public for ibrutinib (2012-13) and acalabrutinib (Byrd 2015) before this mouse PD was public, so retro, not same.
engagement.short: Mouse BTK PD; patients near-complete occupancy
engagement.quote: based on BTK occupancy, 100 mg BID resulted in maximal BTK occupancy with the least inter-patient variability at steady-state trough (Figure 6).
engagement.judgement: Paired: the review reports mouse PD and human occupancy in separate sections without comparing them. Readout counted direct (probe occupancy / ex-vivo BCR blockade). Rescored retro under the retrodiction rule (engagement: any drug of the same target and action counts).

engagement.magnitude_basis: BTK occupancy; mouse values not in abstract
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level for both Tam 2019 and Guo 2019 (model side).
engagement.model: Mouse oral-dose BTK PD (occupancy probe, CD69/CD86)
engagement.note: Zanubrutinib was selected on mouse PD; in patients median PBMC BTK occupancy exceeded 95% at all doses, lymph node occupancy highest at 160 mg BID. Retrodiction rule: patient BTK occupancy for ibrutinib and acalabrutinib was public before Guo 2019, so retro.
engagement.quote: Median BTK occupancy in peripheral blood mononuclear cells was >95% at all doses.
engagement.judgement: Paired with Guo 2019, whose compound selection used in-vivo mouse pharmacodynamics; same mouse-PD track as acalabrutinib. Rescored retro: model first public 2019, after patient BTK occupancy of the same target and action.

engagement.note: QSP model of BTK occupancy in blood, node and marrow built for three covalent BTK inhibitors; opening entry at first use. Track: zanubrutinib; acalabrutinib split to its own entries at the end of the cell.
engagement.quote: The model was developed to describe available clinical BTK occupancy data in patients with B-cell malignancies.
engagement.model: QSP model of tissue BTK occupancy (PBMC, lymph node, marrow)

engagement.magnitude_basis: trough BTK occupancy %, simulated vs observed
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Bone marrow occupancy is a simulation with no clinical counterpart, so only PBMC/LN count.
engagement.note: Fitted and validated on clinical occupancy; reproduced higher trough occupancy for zanubrutinib than acalabrutinib in PBMC and lymph node. Track: zanubrutinib; acalabrutinib split to its own entries at the end of the cell.
engagement.quote: Consistent with observed clinical data, the model predicted that zanubrutinib 160 mg twice daily resulted in higher median trough BTK occupancy in PBMCs, LNs, and BM compared with ibrutinib and acalabrutinib.
engagement.judgement: Retrodiction: built on the clinical occupancy data it reproduces; its PFS link is narrative, so no efficacy entry.
engagement.model: QSP model of tissue BTK occupancy (PBMC, lymph node, marrow)

engagement.note: Acalabrutinib track of the QSP occupancy model, split from the zanubrutinib entry; opening entry at first use.
engagement.quote: This model describes pharmacokinetics of BTK inhibitors; intracellular concentration of BTK inhibitors in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), BM, and lymph nodes (LNs); binding of BTK inhibitors with BTK; and BTK turnover rate.
engagement.judgement: Track split by drug: opening entry for acalabrutinib at model_first_use_year.
engagement.model: QSP model of tissue BTK occupancy (PBMC, lymph node, marrow)

engagement.magnitude_basis: trough BTK occupancy %, simulated vs observed
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Bone marrow occupancy is a simulation with no clinical counterpart, so only PBMC/LN count.
engagement.note: Acalabrutinib track: the QSP model was fitted to and validated on clinical acalabrutinib occupancy, reproducing its lower trough occupancy than zanubrutinib.
engagement.quote: The model was validated using available clinical BTK occupancy data.
engagement.judgement: Track split by drug from engagement 5; retrodiction because the model was built on the clinical occupancy it reproduces.
engagement.model: QSP model of tissue BTK occupancy (PBMC, lymph node, marrow)

dose.model: Mouse oral-dose BTK PD (occupancy probe, CD69/CD86)
dose.note: Mouse PD gave mg/kg ED50s, no human exposure or occupancy target; 100 mg BID was chosen on patient occupancy in ACE-CL-001.
dose.quote: Dose selection was based on results of phase 2 dose-finding Study (ACE-CL-001), which evaluated acalabrutinib dosing regimens of 100 to 400 mg QD and 100 to 200 mg BID
dose.judgement: The BID regimen was hypothesised from short half-life (Byrd 2015) and confirmed clinically; no model-stated exposure target, and an MTD is not a model target.
dose.reason: No human target from the model

dose.model: Mouse oral-dose BTK PD (occupancy probe, CD69/CD86)
dose.note: Zanubrutinib 160 mg BID was chosen for lymph-node occupancy in patients, not from a mouse-derived exposure target.
dose.quote: Sustained complete (>95%) BTK occupancy in lymph node biopsy specimens was more frequent with 160 mg twice daily than 320 mg once daily (89% vs 50%; P = .0342).
dose.judgement: Clinical PD set the regimen; Guo 2019 states no human dose or exposure target in its abstract.
dose.reason: No human target from the model

dose.note: Sponsor Simcyp PBPK model of acalabrutinib filed to set dose with CYP3A modulators; opening entry at first use.
dose.quote: The Applicant developed a physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model of acalabrutinib and its active metabolite ACP-5862 (refer to PBPK review in Appendix for details).
dose.judgement: Opening entry at model_first_use_year; the model's DDI exposure predictions are dose-cell predictions.
dose.model: Sponsor PBPK model (Simcyp) for CYP3A drug-interaction dosing

dose.magnitude_basis: AUC ratio with rifampin, predicted vs observed
dose.population: Healthy volunteers (itraconazole and rifampin DDI studies)
dose.confidence_note: FDA review text; within_2x read from the review's Table 30 statement, not recomputed.
dose.note: fmCYP3A was fitted to the itraconazole study; the model then reproduced the already-run rifampin DDI study in healthy volunteers.
dose.quote: The Acalabrutinib PBPK model was able to predict the observed DDI effects with rifampin (Table 30 and Appendix Figure 2), supporting the estimated value of fmCYP3A.
dose.judgement: Retrodiction: both clinical DDI studies were run before the model was built and used to fit or verify it. Moderate-inhibitor predictions (100 mg QD label) were never tested clinically for acalabrutinib.
dose.model: Sponsor PBPK model (Simcyp) for CYP3A drug-interaction dosing

dose.magnitude_basis: Cmax and AUC, simulated vs observed (pred/obs 0.74-1.23)
dose.population: Healthy volunteers and B-cell malignancy patients
dose.note: Zanubrutinib PBPK reproduced observed PK in volunteers and patients and was verified against the itraconazole and rifampicin DDI study. Same drug own DDI data preceded the model, so the dose retrodiction stands.
dose.quote: The PBPK analyses are adequate to predict the magnitude of the effect of CYP3A4 inhibitors on zanubrutinib exposure.
dose.judgement: Retrodiction (verification against clinical data already in hand). Same PBPK system type as acalabrutinib's, so one track.
dose.model: Sponsor PBPK model (Simcyp) for CYP3A drug-interaction dosing

dose.magnitude_basis: zanubrutinib AUC fold-increase with fluconazole: PBPK ~2.8x (200 mg) vs observed ~1.9x
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; NCT04551963 results posted 2023-11-27. Mixed B-cell histologies, CLL share not checked.
dose.note: Prospective test of the PBPK-based label: 80 mg BID with fluconazole or diltiazem gave exposure comparable to 320 mg QD in patients.
dose.short: PBPK-based DDI doses held in patients
dose.quote: This study supports current United States Prescribing Information dose recommendations for the coadministration of reduced-dose zanubrutinib with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors
dose.judgement: Paired: the moderate-inhibitor regimen in the label rested on PBPK alone; the trial does not cite the model in its abstract. Model over-predicted the interaction slightly, so the reduced dose gave equal, not higher, exposure.
dose.model: Sponsor PBPK model (Simcyp) for CYP3A drug-interaction dosing

efficacy.note: Canine lymphoma responses justified CLL development; ACE-CL-001's primary endpoint was safety, so its 95% ORR does not score.
efficacy.quote: These data, combined with objective clinical responses in a study of naturally occurring canine B-cell lymphomas, provided justification for clinical development of acalabrutinib in CLL.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry: the model's prediction is on record but the first trial's primary endpoint was safety, so it is not an efficacy comparison.

efficacy.confidence_note: Full text (PMC5548968); the paper cites early clinical activity, so it reproduced a known result.
efficacy.model: CLL mouse models (TCL1 adoptive transfer, NSG primary CLL xenograft)
efficacy.note: Acalabrutinib cut tumour burden and prolonged survival in two CLL mouse models, published after patients had responded.
efficacy.short: Mouse CLL benefit, after the clinic
efficacy.quote: In two complementary mouse models of CLL, acalabrutinib significantly reduced tumor burden and increased survival compared to vehicle treatment.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: Byrd 2015 had already reported 95% ORR. Status retro, not same, though no member efficacy-primary trial had yet read out.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: dog ORR 25% vs patient PFS HR 0.31
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Model was canine DLBCL-like lymphoma (cross-histology); dog ORR 25% vs patient benefit large.
efficacy.note: ASCEND: acalabrutinib monotherapy beat idelalisib-R/bendamustine-R on IRC-assessed PFS in relapsed CLL (HR 0.31). Retrodiction rule: the canine data were first public in 2014, after ibrutinib CLL responses (Byrd 2013), so retro. Dated to the 7 May 2019 AstraZeneca press release that ASCEND met its PFS primary endpoint. ALPINE (zanubrutinib) removed from patient_trials: another drug, not on this acalabrutinib track.
efficacy.quote: Acalabrutinib significantly improved PFS compared with I-R or B-R and has an acceptable safety profile in patients with R/R CLL.
efficacy.judgement: Paired with Harrington 2016. The dogs predicted activity only, so magnitude direction_only. ELEVATE-TN (2020, PFS) and SEQUOIA/ALPINE (zanubrutinib) also positive; listed in patient_trials. Rescored retro under the retrodiction rule; year moved to the earliest public date (press release).

patient_trials.quote: Acalabrutinib with or without obinutuzumab significantly improved progression-free survival over obinutuzumab-chlorambucil chemoimmunotherapy, providing a chemotherapy-free treatment option with an acceptable side-effect profile that was consistent with previous studies.

safety.magnitude_basis: absence of AF/major bleeding vs ibrutinib history
safety.confidence_note: Full text (PMC4862586); uncontrolled, n=61, 14 months follow-up. Quote is two adjacent sentences (31 words).
safety.model: Kinase selectivity panel and ex-vivo platelet/NK assays vs ibrutinib
safety.note: Selectivity and intact platelet aggregation predicted fewer ibrutinib-type harms; 61 relapsed CLL patients had no major hemorrhage or atrial fibrillation.
safety.short: No AF or major bleeding, phase 1-2
safety.quote: Furthermore, in patients receiving ibrutinib, we demonstrate diminished platelet aggregation, whereas with acalabrutinib we do not observe this. This finding may reflect why major bleeding events with acalabrutinib have, thus far, not occurred.
safety.judgement: Single-arm, short follow-up; scored same because the source states model and patient results together. Headache (43%) was a harm the assays were silent on but could not show.

safety.population: Previously treated CLL with del(17p) or del(11q) (ELEVATE-RR)
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; bleeding rates not checked in full text.
safety.model: Kinase selectivity panel and ex-vivo platelet/NK assays vs ibrutinib
safety.note: ELEVATE-RR head-to-head: AF/flutter 9.4% vs 16.0% with ibrutinib; fewer cardiovascular events and discontinuations, but AF not abolished.
safety.short: Less AF than ibrutinib, not none
safety.quote: In this first direct comparison of less versus more selective Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors in CLL, acalabrutinib demonstrated noninferior PFS with fewer cardiovascular adverse events.
safety.judgement: Partial: the 2015 reading suggested no AF, the randomised trial showed less AF rather than none. Stated by the trial authors as a test of the selectivity hypothesis.

safety.model: Kinase selectivity panel and ex-vivo platelet/NK assays vs ibrutinib
safety.note: ALPINE: zanubrutinib, selected for selectivity over TEC/EGFR, had fewer cardiac events than ibrutinib in relapsed CLL. Dated to the 28 Apr 2021 BeiGene press release of the ALPINE interim analysis (AF/flutter 2.5% vs 10.1%); NEJM 2022 is the tier-1 source.
safety.quote: The safety profile of zanubrutinib was better than that of ibrutinib, with fewer adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation and fewer cardiac events, including fewer cardiac events leading to treatment discontinuation or death.
safety.judgement: Paired: ALPINE cites greater specificity but does not tie it to Guo 2019's panel, so comparison_stated false.

safety.magnitude_basis: dog/rat tox: no bleeding signal, platelet aggregation unremarkable, toxicities limited to RBC/albumin changes; patients: ~50% any bleeding
safety.population: Pooled B-cell malignancy safety set (n=612) including CLL patients
safety.confidence_note: FDA review text (bundle), both halves. Tox quote: "Toxicities were limited to changes in clinical pathology consisting of reversible effects on red blood cell parameters including decreases in red cell mass and decreases in albumin." Rat lethal-dose cardiac hemorrhage is a lesion, not a bleeding tendency.
safety.model: Rat and dog GLP repeat-dose toxicology
safety.note: Tolerability ruling: rat/dog tox stated toxicities limited to reversible RBC and albumin changes, dog platelet aggregation unremarkable; ~50% of patients bled (any grade). Retrodiction: own CLL patient data public 2015.
safety.short: Tox findings not compared in patients
safety.quote: In the combined safety database (n=612), overall bleeding events, including bruising and petechiae of any grade, occurred in approximately 50% of patients.
safety.judgement: Rule question settled under the tolerability ruling: the tox statement is a safety prediction; dogs can show bleeding (zanubrutinib dogs did), so the silence is contradicted. Retrodiction (tox first public 2017, after Byrd 2015), failed to reproduce: contra.
safety.reason: Tox silent on bleeding; patients bled

safety.magnitude_basis: hemorrhage in rat/dog repeat-dose tox vs any bleeding (~50%) and major hemorrhage (3%) in the pooled B-cell malignancy safety set
safety.population: Pooled B-cell malignancy safety set (n=629) including CLL patients
safety.confidence_note: FDA review text (bundle). Patient side is a pooled B-cell malignancy safety set (n=629) incl. CLL, CLL share not separated; the review lists hemorrhage among events chosen from preclinical findings and class effects but does not credit the animal finding alone.
safety.note: Zanubrutinib rat/dog tox showed multi-organ hemorrhage and bleeding-related RBC loss; patients had ~50% any bleeding and 3% major hemorrhage. Retrodiction rule (safety, same drug): the tox was first public in the Nov 2019 review, after zanubrutinib own patient bleeding data (phase 1, Tam 2019), so retro.
safety.quote: Events of clinical interest were identified based on preclinical findings, data from clinical studies, and pharmacological effects associated with BTK inhibitors, including hemorrhage, infections, cytopenias, atrial fibrillation or flutter, and second primary malignancies.
safety.judgement: Paired within one review: the nonclinical section reports multi-organ hemorrhage in rat and dog, the clinical section ~50% bleeding; direction matched, so same. Zanubrutinib's sponsor tox placed on the existing rat-dog-glp-tox track (same system type; cross-sponsor question open). Rescored retro: post-dating by first public date makes it a retrodiction whatever the run date.
safety.model: Rat and dog GLP repeat-dose toxicology
